name: dispatch
algorithm: n dynamic calls through a two-element array of {context pointer, inline function pointer} pairs (Mk: gen dyn.Of's StepDyn) over an Add and a Xor, the target picked by bit 0 of a splitmix64 stream and the argument its upper 63 bits; the results summed with wrapping arithmetic (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the algorithm already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24: no data-dependent control flow besides the dispatch target, which is the checksum's input; the trip count is n, and the checksum is exact wrapping integer arithmetic over the whole sequence of targets and arguments
notes: Dispatch values, one data structure (C's {context pointer, function pointer} pair, the fn inline): C {void *self; fn pointer}; Zig {*anyopaque, *const fn}; Rust {&mut Acc, fn pointer} and Go {*Acc, func value}, both objects one Acc type since safe Rust and Go cannot erase a pointer's type; Mk gen dyn.Of(Step)'s StepDyn (a dyn.Ref, the address and the type key, and the fn inline; the adapter compares the key before the direct call). Go's func value points to a closure record, one dependent load more, which Go cannot avoid. Review finding DYN-6 moved Rust (&mut dyn), Zig (vtable pointer) and Go (interface) off their native vtable-pointer values, which are a different data structure.

Written by the std-dyn lane (status/std-dyn.md). Checksums: from the earlier columns' verified runs (all columns agreed, 2026-11-07) and a Go reference of the pseudo-code; the reworked columns are reverified through tools/bench verify (status/std-dyn.md audit table).
